rule_rows.note: Implements the FICO- and transaction-specific CLTV check for loans of $1,500,000 or less. It rejects higher loan amounts rather than checking the other loan-amount tier, so it does not implement the full published matrix check.
The rule selects matrix CLTV limits by loan amount, FICO, and purpose, but does not compare CLTV against the selected limit or complete handling for all matrix entries.
Checks that positive rental income for a vacant-property purchase uses a 1007 or 1025, but does not verify that the required 1007 survey is present.
The rule checks short-term-rental CLTV/FICO limits and low-or-no-ratio CLTV caps, but does not implement the jobs’ other documentation, scope, or condition checks.

The rule bypasses DSCR calculation for No Ratio files and applies several situation-specific minimums. It does not check the No Ratio documentation, cap, or insurance requirements, and it omits the mixed-use minimum and other qualifications in job 14.

The rule partially handles citizenship categories and applies the Foreign National FICO and CLTV checks. It does not implement the documentation requirements or escrow-waiver check, and it returns false for Permanent Residents and Non-Permanent Residents. The ITIN branch is truncated before any limits are checked.
Checks the requirement that scores and tradelines are reported under the correct ITIN or SSN, which is one part of job 3.
Checks only that the loan purpose is business purpose; it does not check the other foreign-national eligibility requirements.
Checks the business-purpose investment-property condition for entity borrowers, but not the full entity, ownership, title, or guarantee requirements.
Checks allowed entity type and prior-homeownership attestation from job 23, plus entity-document completeness from job 22; it does not implement all checks in either job.
The rule checks whether required entity documentation is complete, matching job 22.
The rule checks entity document completeness, which duplicates job 22’s entity documentation check.
Implements the printed label- and purpose-specific CLTV limits, including treating Ineligible as ineligible. It does not check that Acra has confirmed label definitions or seasoning.
Checks that the property type is eligible, but does not implement the above-80% LTV restriction.

The rule checks the >80% CLTV property limitation and rural-property CLTV, FICO, and DSCR requirements. It does not check reserves or account for possible further LTV reductions for unusual properties, so it only partially implements these jobs.
The rule returns the six-month listing-period flag but does not check the listed-property loan conditions.
Implements the stated ≤70% CLTV exemption check, but not the other rent loss insurance requirements in job 50.

Checks the interest-only loan amount and FICO requirements, and also applies the first-time-homebuyer and vacant-property-refinance restrictions. The rule does not cover every requirement in those broader jobs.
The rule checks state-specific prepayment penalty buy-out restrictions. None of the listed jobs states that check.
The rule applies the published matrix CLTV limits by loan amount, FICO, and transaction type, matching job 37.

Implements the published minimum-FICO-by-loan-amount check, including the purchase-only condition for scores 620–639 in the $1,500,001–$2,000,000 band. It does not check the other program-scope requirements.

Implements job 33’s delayed-financing cap. It checks the 1007 requirement only for 2–4-unit DSCR files (job 42) and the 15-month ownership condition only for vacant rate-and-term refinances (job 52), so those jobs are only partially covered.
Implements the job’s check for FICO below 600 when the loan amount is $1,500,000 or less.
Checks the published program-level scope, including amount, credit, leverage, DSCR, borrower, property, and state requirements.
The rule checks the stated $1.5MM delayed-financing cap, which is listed under both job 33 and job 54.
Checks the loan amount range and $50 increments, seller-contribution limit, and that the property state is not SD.

rule_rows.note: The rule implements the 75% loan-amount CLTV cap, the delayed-financing $1.5MM cap, and Correspondent 700–719 CLTV limits. It covers only parts of those jobs: it omits other amount and matrix checks, and it applies a 55% cash-out limit at FICO 720 rather than leaving that treatment unsettled pending confirmation.
Checks only the exclusion of short-term rentals, which is one part of job 16.
The rule checks the channel-specific DSCR minimum stated in both jobs, but does not implement their other checks.

The rule checks the cash-out lease requirement and the first-time homebuyer restriction. It accepts US citizens but rejects Permanent Residents rather than checking their required documentation, so the citizenship requirements are only partially implemented.

The rule fully checks that the applicant is not a first-time homebuyer and checks the listed citizenship exclusions. It does not verify US-citizen or permanent-resident status or the required permanent-resident documents, so it only partially implements job 10.
Checks the printed “0x30x12” housing-history requirement, but not the previous-credit-event seasoning requirement.
The rule applies the stated eligible types, rural-property exclusion, and 75% CLTV limit, but rejects all unlisted property types instead of treating them as not addressed.

The rule checks the excluded locations, property-type exclusions and stated CLTV caps, and rejects vacant properties. It does not apply the declining-market CLTV reduction, assess occupancy requirements, or preserve the not-addressed status of property types.
Checks only the stated ≤70% CLTV exemption from rent loss insurance.
Checks only whether CLTV exceeds 70%; it does not evaluate the transaction type or the business-purpose funds-to-close condition in the seasoning-verification trigger.
The rule repeats both PLAT-9.3 and PLAT-9.5 checks in job 39.
Checks the six-month listed-for-sale flag and identifies the three-year minimum, but cannot verify the requested penalty or state exception.

Implements the stated FICO-band and Correspondent CLTV caps, plus applicable CLTV caps for loan amount, property type, and listed-for-sale status. It does not cover every requirement in these jobs, such as decisioning-score selection, the exact-720 confirmation, property eligibility determinations, or the full listed-for-sale test.

Implements the FICO floor, purpose-based CLTV limits, amount-triggered 75% cap, and Correspondent 700–719 CLTV restriction. It does not implement the full decisioning-score selection or all amount and CLTV requirements in those jobs.
Checks the $1.5MM delayed-financing loan cap, which is one part of job 29.
Checks the not-vacant requirement, which is one check in each listed job.
Checks only that the property is not vacant, which is one check within each job.
Repeats the delayed-financing $1.5MM loan-amount cap check stated in both jobs.
The rule repeats the six-month reserves check for CLTV above 75.00%.

The rule checks eligible citizenship status, non-first-time-homebuyer status, and non-vacancy, but omits other requirements in those jobs. The Short-Term Rental exclusion is not stated in the listed jobs.
Implements the stated CLTV caps for FICO 730+, channel-specific minimum DSCR, and location exclusions. It does not implement the other checks described in those jobs.
Checks the Non-Owner Occupied condition in both jobs, but not their other requirements.
Repeats job 43’s purpose, vacancy, delayed-financing cap, and cash-out lease checks. The channel-specific DSCR thresholds are not stated by any listed job.
The rule duplicates job 28: it enforces the loan amount minimum, maximum, and $50 increments, plus the 75% CLTV cap for amounts below $350,000 or above $1,500,000.

The rule applies the matrix CLTV limits, but it treats exactly 720 as settled under the 700 row, contrary to job 30’s confirmation requirement, and omits that job’s other stated caps. It also checks only the $2,000,000 upper loan-amount bound from job 29, not the minimum, $50 increments, or delayed-financing limit.
